## Purpose

Read one stored morning report: its window, state, finalization reason and the
authored or fallback content that separates landed changes, pending shipment,
failures and source gaps.

## When a playbook uses it

A step that has a report id (from `morning_report_tick` or `report_list`) and needs
its content, for example to relay or summarize it. The dashboard's
`/reports/:id` page and `aq report show ID` read the same command.

## How it works internally

`src/commands/report_commands.py` loads the row with `get_morning_report` and
checks visibility: an enforced principal with no project and no elevation sees
nothing; a project principal sees a report only when its project was configured
or appears in the brief. A project-scoped read keeps that project's section only,
drops global facts and git, provider and digest gaps belonging to other scopes,
and rewrites the summary. `is_fallback` is true when no authored report exists or
the row finalized as `author_deadline` or `no_changes`.

## Side effects and persistence

None. Reports are immutable once terminal and retained for 90 days after
finalization.

## Failure modes and diagnostics

`not_found` covers both a missing id and a report outside the caller's scope, so
the refusal does not reveal other projects' reports. `aq report list` shows the
ids the caller may read.

## Example step

```yaml
id: read-morning
kind: command
command: report_get
args:
  report_id: morning-2026-09-25
```
